checks: the controlled instruction string appeared in each native-client transcript, demonstrating that returned JSON was passed through

limits: This is evidence of an open server-side prompt-injection quarantine gap: valid JSON instructions are returned to clients as untrusted content, not sanitized or isolated.

The explicit user prompt told each client to treat the payload as data; two successful finite sessions do not prove that a model will always resist prompt injection or that it did not use any other unobserved tool in another context.
No real secret, public target, packet or syscall trace was involved. Traffic sent through other tools remains outside Outbound Guard.
Cursor was not rerun under its plan gate. The Debian installer is unsigned with signed build provenance. No official candidate or stable release is approved.
